core_meaning.primary_meaning: Abidah corresponds to Arabic عابدة, the feminine form of عابد (“worshipper/devotee”); “of God” is contextual rather than an explicit element of the word.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The recorded form عابدة is the feminine form related to عابد (“worshipper/devotee”). The earlier translations that use masculine عابد/عبد or add a separate “of God” element are corrected.

etymology.morphology: Feminine active participle (fāʿilah pattern, feminine of عابد) of عَبَدَ, built on the root ع ب د.
etymology.etymological_meaning: From the root ع ب د (ʿ-b-d)
etymology.etymology_explanation: The form عابدة is an established Arabic lexical item — the feminine of عابد (ʿābid) — and Abidah is the word itself used as a personal name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: No derivation beyond the documented Arabic form is asserted. Any etymology that attributes this spelling to a different root or language without a source should be treated as unverified.

islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: Muslim use of the name is not evidence that the word is Qur'anic or religiously prescribed.
